project.description_en: At the end of the theme, the child takes part in a small class celebration: helps to decorate, sings or dances, says thank you for a gift and shows the flag of Cameroon.

activities.goal_en: Say a counting rhyme and count down with the fingers.
activities.prompt_en: Let us say the candle rhyme and count with our fingers.
steps_en: Show ten fingers as ten candles.
Say the rhyme, folding one finger each time.
Say it together.
Count the fingers left at the end.
observe_en: Folds one finger at a time.
source_refs: Nursery One, table 15 (Poetry and Rhymes: Rhymes), p. 40; theme 4: Festivities/Celebrations (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery One contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery One teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.story_en:
Ten little candles on a birthday cake,
Blow, blow, blow, one goes out, for goodness’ sake!
Nine little candles… (go on to one)
No more candles, let us eat the cake!

activities.goal_en: Show surprise and happiness without words.
activities.prompt_en: Without speaking, show me: you open a present and you are surprised and happy!
steps_en: Show a surprised face: eyes and mouth wide open.
Show a happy face with clapping.
Mime opening a present.
The others guess what happened.
observe_en: Guesses the mime of a friend.
source_refs: Nursery One, table 16 (Sign Language and Gestures: Facial expressions), p. 41; theme 4: Festivities/Celebrations (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery One contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery One teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.goal_en: Draw waves and curves for a party garland.
activities.prompt_en: Let us draw a garland for the party: up and down, like waves.
steps_en: Move the arm like a wave in the air.
Trace waves on a long strip of paper.
Add small curves like balloons.
Colour the garland and hang it.
observe_en: Keeps the waves on the line.
source_refs: Nursery One, table 18 (Writing: Pre-letter formation), p. 43; theme 4: Festivities/Celebrations (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery One contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery One teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.goal_en: Say the days of the week in French with help.
activities.prompt_en: In French, the days are: lundi, mardi, mercredi, jeudi, vendredi, samedi, dimanche.
steps_en: Say the days slowly, clapping once for each day.
The child repeats with you.
Say the day of the party: “La fête, c’est samedi !”
Point to a calendar while saying the days.
observe_en: Repeats the days in order with help.
source_refs: Nursery One, table 19 (French: Jours de la semaine), p. 44; theme 4: Festivities/Celebrations (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery One contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery One teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.prompt_en: How many candles are on this cake? Let us count.
steps_en: Draw a cake or use a play-dough cake.
Put sticks as candles: 6 to 10.
Touch and count each candle.
Say the total and make it change.
materials_en: play dough or a drawing of a cake
source_refs: Nursery One, table 20 (Mathematics: Counting), p. 45; theme 4: Festivities/Celebrations (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery One contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery One teacher of the English subsystem.

interactive.prompt_en: How many candles are on the cake?
interactive.explanation_en: Touch each candle and count: there are 7 candles.

activities.goal_en: Take away one or two objects and say how many are left, within 10.
activities.prompt_en: There are 5 balloons. Pop! One balloon bursts. How many are left?
steps_en: Show 5 balloons (or circles).
Take one away: “Pop!”.
Count the balloons left.
Try with other numbers up to 10.
source_refs: Nursery One, table 20 (Mathematics: Mathematical operations), p. 45; theme 4: Festivities/Celebrations (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery One contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery One teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.goal_en: Differentiate good and bad smells and link bad smells with dirt to clean.
activities.prompt_en: Smell gently. Is it a good smell or a bad smell?
steps_en: Prepare a flower, an orange peel and soap (good smells).
Say that bad smells come from rubbish or a dirty toilet.
The child smells the good things gently.
Ask: what do we do when there is a bad smell? (clean, throw rubbish away)
observe_en: Gives one way to remove a bad smell.
source_refs: Nursery One, table 21 (Sensory and Perceptive Education: The sense of smell), p. 46; theme 4: Festivities/Celebrations (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery One contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery One teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.goal_en: Recognise the flag of Cameroon and show respect for it.
activities.prompt_en: This is our flag: green, red with a yellow star, and yellow. We stand still when the flag goes up.
steps_en: Show the flag or a picture of it.
Name the colours together: green, red, yellow, and the star.
Explain that on national days we celebrate with the flag.
Practise standing still for the flag.
materials_en: a small flag of Cameroon or a picture
source_refs: Nursery One, table 24 (Citizenship: National emblems and officials), p. 50; theme 4: Festivities/Celebrations (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery One contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery One teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.goal_en: Show appreciation and share with others at a party.
activities.prompt_en: When we receive a present, we say thank you. We also share our sweets with our friends.
steps_en: Act: give the child a small wrapped present.
The child says “Thank you!” and smiles.
Give a few biscuits and ask the child to share them.
Talk about how sharing makes friends happy.
observe_en: Says thank you without being reminded.
Shows empathy for a friend who has nothing.
source_refs: Nursery One, table 25 (Character Education: Good behaviour), p. 51; theme 4: Festivities/Celebrations (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery One contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery One teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.title_en: At the party: water and fruit
activities.goal_en: Choose the right drink and avoid too many sugary foods.
activities.prompt_en: At a party, we eat fruit, we drink water and we take only a little sweet food.
steps_en: Show pictures of party food: fruit, water, juice, sweets, cake.
Sort them: every day / only a little.
Talk about teeth and sugar.
Prepare a fruit plate together.
observe_en: Says that sweets are “only a little”.
source_refs: Nursery One, table 28 (Health Education and Nutrition: Good health habits), p. 54; theme 4: Festivities/Celebrations (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery One contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery One teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.goal_en: Show at least one Cameroonian dance step with the rhythm.
activities.prompt_en: Listen to the drum. Let us learn one step: step to the right, step to the left, and turn!
steps_en: Clap or beat the rhythm on a drum.
Show a simple step on the beat (for example a makossa or bikutsi step).
The child copies slowly, then with the music.
Dance together in a circle.
observe_en: Dances with joy in the group.
source_refs: Nursery One, table 29 (Music and Dance: Traditional music and dance), p. 55; theme 4: Festivities/Celebrations (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery One contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery One teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.goal_en: Walk with confidence on a catwalk and encourage friends.
activities.prompt_en: Walk along the line like at a fashion parade, stop, turn and smile. Then clap for your friend!
steps_en: Mark a straight line on the floor.
Walk along it slowly, head up.
Stop at the end, turn and walk back.
The others clap for each friend.
observe_en: Walks on the line with balance.
source_refs: Nursery One, table 32 (Physical Education and Sports: Team sports), p. 58; theme 4: Festivities/Celebrations (table 13, p. 37)

scale.description: Succeeds mostly with a model or help.
Sometimes succeeds alone, sometimes with a reminder.
Succeeds on their own in a familiar situation.

indicators: Takes away 1 or 2 from a small group.
Says thank you for a gift.
Chooses water rather than too many sweets.
Says the days of the week in French with help.

sources: Cameroon Nursery School Curriculum, English Subsystem, MINEDUB, 2018: table 13 (integrated learning themes), p. 37; Nursery One tables, cited and not reproduced.
